name: Agosta-class SSK (Agosta, S620; Ouessant photographed)

published.source: en.wikipedia 'Agosta-class submarine' raw wikitext read 2026-11-26: length 67 m (France, Spain), beam 6 m; no draught given

references.name: [G1] Ouessant (S623) surfaced off Brest, 2005, port broadside
references.note: Port broadside, bow LEFT (flipped). Bow x 35, upper rudder's after edge x 730: 695 px = the published 67 m, 10.37 px/m; her waterline row 312: X = (382.5 - px) / 10.37, Z = (312 - py) / 10.37. A photograph at a distance, nearly level: the casing 2.1 m out of the water, the sail X 6.5 .. 16.6 to 10.9, two masts raised, the dark opening at the sail's forward foot (px 214 .. 225, rows 255 .. 287), the pale line along the casing's side 0.9 m up, the upper rudder standing clear abaft the casing (X -30.5 .. -33.5). Kept as "quarter" (no outline is taken: the background mask picks up the shore and the sky) with an overlay block, so overlay.py lays the render on it; the landmarks below are read off it (view side). In the overlay the casing abaft X -17 lies lower than the model's by up to 0.8 m, in spray and broken water: not used.

references.name: [G2] Agosta (S620) alongside at Rouen, 1994, starboard
references.note: For the reviewer: the boat herself from the starboard bow quarter: the same sail with its seam round it about 4 m up, the flat casing, the bow plane low on the bow, the matt black steel.

must_show: hull 67 m (bow X +33.5 to the upper rudder's after edge X -33.5; the screw just beyond), beam 6 m, the casing's flat deck 2.1 m out of the water from X -15 to 27, falling to the bow and the stern
the casing on the hull's back, its sides sloping down to the water, the pale strake along them 0.9 m up X -14 .. 25 [G1]; a row of limber holes low on them

the tall sail X 6.4 .. 16.8, top 10.9 m, front and back near upright, the top edges rounded; the seam round it at 4.0 m [G1][G2]; the dark opening at its forward foot X 14.6 .. 15.5, z 2.4 .. 5.5 [G1]; the bridge windows and recess at the top front X 14.3 .. 16.0; the periscope standard and masts raised X 12.6 .. 14.0 [G1]; ladder rungs
the bow planes low on the bow X 29.3 .. 31.3 at z 0.6, 2.2 m out [G2]

cruciform stern: the upper rudder X -33.5 .. -29.4 at its root standing clear of the water to 2.1 m, its leading edge meeting the water at X -29.9 [G1], the lower rudder and stern planes (3.6 m out) under water, hinge slots; the five-bladed screw on its shaft fairing at X -33.85

weld seams round the pressure hull every 4 m; hatches X -12, 3.5, 21 and the loading hatch X 26; cleats; capstan X 28; the safety track; bow shutters X 32; plain matt black steel, no numbers or markings; team colour only as small strips

landmarks.name: upper rudder leading edge at the water
landmarks.note: [G1] the leading edge meets the water at px 693 (review 1)

not_confirmed: everything under the water: the keel at -4.8 (published beam plus the casing), the lower rudder, the stern planes' span, the screw (here aft of the cruciform), the torpedo shutters' places
the knuckle (drawn at z 0.0) and the casing deck's width (3.4 m): no end view
the sail's width (2.8 m), its plan; the window places
the limber row's places; the hatches' places
